rejected.description: The episode-start detector uses the debounced SCR readback latch_state where the accumulator uses the CPLD's latch_assert, so a CPLD trip opens no episode until the readback follows
The episode start time is latched from the two low bytes of timestamp_ms only, as if the counter were 16 bits wide, so the top byte of fault_time is always zero
rejected.why: make lint already catches it: make lint: UNUSEDSIGNAL

runs.reason: equivalent: fault_reg and fault_time are set on the same clock (episode_start is the accumulator's first capture) and cleared on the same read, so an empty fault_reg always has fault_time 0 and skipping its clear changes nothing
descriptions: fault_time is cleared by a host read only when the record is non-empty, on the belief that an empty record has no start time to clear

runs.reason: another relabelling of the cause bit map; the adjacent swaps AIM.36, AIM.38, AIM.47 and AIM.49 already move every cause, and any test that checks each cause on its own bit kills them all
descriptions: Cause bit positions laid out LSB-first (OVP in bit 0, OVERCURRENT in bit 4), with the priority order misremembered as LSB highest
Over-voltage and over-current are confused in the bit map: OVP is placed in bit 0 and OVERCURRENT in bit 4
The two overcurrent-related causes are confused in the bit map: LATCH_ASSERT (OCP/SCP) is placed in bit 0 and the window-trip OVERCURRENT in bit 3
Over-voltage and under-voltage are confused in the bit map: OVP is placed in bit 1 and UVLO in bit 4
OVP and OTP, acronyms one letter apart, are swapped in the bit map: over-temperature is reported in bit 4 and the inferred overvoltage in bit 2
Over-temperature (OT) and over-current (OC) are confused in the bit map: OTP is placed in bit 0 and OVERCURRENT in bit 2
The two lock-type causes are confused in the bit map: the CPLD latch trip (LATCH_ASSERT) is placed in bit 1 and under-voltage lockout (UVLO) in bit 3

runs.reason: no test raises two causes on the same clock: each cause is recorded alone, so a cause masked by another live cause goes unseen; needs simultaneous pairs of causes with every bit checked

no test adds a cause after another is already recorded in the orders that matter (UVLO second, a lower-priority cause after a higher one, OVP after any cause); needs causes arriving in several orders, each checked to be added

no cause is raised during soft start: OTP, UVLO and OVP captured in S_SS, the episode stamp from S_SS and a second cause in S_SS are untested; needs causes in S_SS with fault_reg and fault_time checked

nothing is raised while the converter is stopped: the header says a fault asserting while stopped is not captured and the record holds until read, but no test raises latch_state, latch_assert or OTP (or lets OTP clear) with the converter stopped and checks fault_reg and fault_time stay as they were
host reads are only tested while running with causes gone: a read on the clock the first cause is captured, a read while stopped, and a read of an empty record with a cause live are untested
an episode opened by OVP alone and a UVLO record surviving a later soft start are untested; needs an OVP-only record followed by a second cause (fault_time held), and a restart after a recorded UVLO
differs only for an episode stamped while timestamp_ms is 0: the 24-bit ms counter is 0 for 1 ms after reset (the converter cannot be running yet) and for 1 ms every 4.66 h after it wraps

The LATCH_ASSERT bit is therefore never set on the chip - a design note, see the finding

AIM.1.description: On a host read, capture wins over clear: fault_reg is loaded with the causes live on that clock instead of being emptied
AIM.1.reason: A read landing while a cause is live and the converter is running leaves fault_reg non-empty on the next clock instead of zero, and because fault_reg never passes through empty, fault_time stays at 0 instead of re-latching the new episode's start time.

judgements.reason: fault_reg_read_done can pulse while fault_reg is empty and a cause is live while running. Then episode_start is also true and the mutant stamps fault_time where the original clears it.

decisions.reason: host reads are only tested while running with causes gone: a read on the clock the first cause is captured, a read while stopped, and a read of an empty record with a cause live are untested

AIM.2.description: fault_time capture takes priority over its clear-on-read, the opposite of fault_reg
AIM.2.before: else if (fault_reg_read_done)     fault_time <= '0; / else if (episode_start)           fault_time <= timestamp_ms;
AIM.2.after: else if (episode_start)           fault_time <= timestamp_ms; / else if (fault_reg_read_done)     fault_time <= '0;
AIM.2.reason: When a host read lands on the clock a first cause appears in an empty fault_reg, fault_time takes timestamp_ms while fault_reg stays empty; if the cause was gone by the next clock, fault_time is left non-zero beside an empty fault_reg.

AIM.3.description: Episode start is detected from fault_reg having gone non-empty rather than from the capture conditions, so fault_time is latched one clock after the first cause
AIM.3.before: episode_start = convertor_running && (fault_reg == '0) / && (otp_state || uvlo_state || ovp || latch_assert / || window_trip || window_trip_SS);
AIM.3.reason: fault_time is still 0 on the clock fault_reg first shows a cause and takes the timestamp one clock later, which is the next millisecond's value when the first cause arrives on the clock before timestamp_ms increments.

judgements.reason: If the episode is stamped when timestamp_ms=0, fault_time stays 0 while fault_reg is non-empty. A later cause then re-stamps fault_time in the mutant; it also stamps whenever fault_time is 0 even though fault_reg is non-empty.

decisions.reason: differs only for an episode stamped while timestamp_ms is 0: the 24-bit ms counter is 0 for 1 ms after reset (the converter cannot be running yet) and for 1 ms every 4.66 h after it wraps

AIM.4.description: The episode is judged empty by fault_time being zero instead of fault_reg being zero
AIM.4.reason: An episode that begins while timestamp_ms is 0 (the first millisecond after reset, or after the counter wraps) does not hold its start time: fault_time is overwritten with the later timestamp while any cause is still live after the counter moves on.

AIM.5.description: OVP is inferred against the recorded LATCH bit instead of the live latch_assert
AIM.5.reason: A CPLD-originated trip with latch_assert and latch_state both high and LATCH not yet recorded (the first clock, or after a host read) falsely sets the OVP bit, and a real analog OVP trip after an unread earlier CPLD trip is not recorded.

AIM.6.description: Over-temperature bypasses the capture gate: with otp_state high, causes are recorded even while the converter is stopped
AIM.6.reason: With ss_active and run_active both low, otp_state high sets the OTP bit (and any other live cause's bit, such as UVLO during power-down) in fault_reg where it should stay empty, with fault_time left at 0.

judgements.reason: A UVLO during ss_active only sets BIT_UVLO in the original but not in the mutant.

decisions.reason: no cause is raised during soft start: OTP, UVLO and OVP captured in S_SS, the episode stamp from S_SS and a second cause in S_SS are untested; needs causes in S_SS with fault_reg and fault_time checked

AIM.7.description: UVLO is recorded only in S_RUN; a UVLO that interrupts soft start is forgotten
AIM.7.reason: With ss_active high and uvlo_state asserted, the UVLO bit of fault_reg stays 0 while fault_time still latches a timestamp for an episode with no cause in it.

AIM.8.description: The clear-on-read leaves the OVP bit set; only the four lower cause bits are cleared
AIM.8.reason: After an inferred OVP has been recorded, a host read leaves fault_reg at 5'b10000 instead of 0, so every later read reports OVP until reset and later episodes never see an empty register to latch a new fault_time.

AIM.9.description: A host read clears only the recorded causes that have gone away; a recorded cause still asserted survives the read, even with the converter stopped
AIM.9.after: fault_reg <= fault_reg & {ovp, latch_assert, otp_state, uvlo_state, (window_trip || window_trip_SS)};
AIM.9.reason: With the converter stopped after a fault and the condition still present (UVLO still low, OTP still hot), a read leaves that bit set in fault_reg where the original returns to 0 and stays there because capture is gated off.

judgements.reason: If otp_state and uvlo_state are both high while running, the else-if chain records only BIT_OTP on that clock. A one-clock UVLO is lost.

decisions.reason: no test raises two causes on the same clock: each cause is recorded alone, so a cause masked by another live cause goes unseen; needs simultaneous pairs of causes with every bit checked

AIM.10.description: Causes are captured through a priority chain, one per clock, instead of independently accumulated
AIM.10.before: if(uvlo_state)                      fault_reg[BIT_UVLO]  <= 1'b1; / if(window_trip || window_trip_SS)   fault_reg [BIT_OC]   <= 1'b1; / if(ovp)                             fault_reg[BIT_OVP]   <= 1'b1; / if(latch_assert)                    fault_reg[BIT_LATCH] <= 1'b1;
AIM.10.after: else if(uvlo_state)                 fault_reg[BIT_UVLO]  <= 1'b1; / else if(window_trip || window_trip_SS) fault_reg [BIT_OC] <= 1'b1; / else if(ovp)                        fault_reg[BIT_OVP]   <= 1'b1; / else if(latch_assert)               fault_reg[BIT_LATCH] <= 1'b1;
AIM.10.reason: When two causes are live together while the converter is running (for example otp_state with uvlo_state, or window_trip with latch_assert), only the first in the chain is recorded and the other bit of fault_reg stays 0 for as long as the first remains asserted.

AIM.11.description: The OVERCURRENT bit follows the live window trips while running instead of being set and held
AIM.11.reason: If the window trip deasserts while ss_active or run_active is still high, bit 0 of fault_reg drops back to 0 before the host has read it, so a transient overcurrent is no longer reported.

AIM.12.description: A host read clears fault_reg only when the converter is stopped; a read during S_SS or S_RUN does not clear it
AIM.12.reason: Reading the register while ss_active or run_active is high leaves the earlier causes in fault_reg although the cause conditions are gone, while fault_time is cleared to 0, so the record keeps stale bits with no start time.

AIM.13.description: latch_assert also sets the OVERCURRENT bit, on the assumption that every CPLD latch trip is an overcurrent
AIM.13.reason: With latch_assert high and neither window trip asserted while the converter is running, fault_reg reads 5'b01001 instead of 5'b01000.

AIM.14.description: The episode start is detected only in S_RUN: a first cause captured during soft start does not latch fault_time
AIM.14.reason: With ss_active high and run_active low, a first cause sets its fault_reg bit but fault_time stays 0, and stays 0 for the rest of the episode because fault_reg is no longer empty.

judgements.reason: While running, if latch_state=1, latch_assert=0 and window_trip=1, the mutant leaves ovp low. fault_reg[BIT_OVP] is then not set at line 208, so the output differs.

decisions.reason: no test raises two causes on the same clock: each cause is recorded alone, so a cause masked by another live cause goes unseen; needs simultaneous pairs of causes with every bit checked

AIM.15.description: OVP inference is suppressed while an overcurrent window trip is live, on the assumption that the latch trip then belongs to the overcurrent
AIM.15.reason: An analog trip (latch_state high, latch_assert low) that coincides with window_trip or window_trip_SS while running sets only the OVERCURRENT bit; fault_reg[4] is never set.

judgements.reason: With BIT_OVP already recorded, a later latch_assert while running clears BIT_OVP in the mutant. The original keeps it set.

decisions.reason: need latch_assert high while the converter runs, which never happens on the chip: strike_counter raises latch_assert on hiccup entry, after S_RUN has been left, and the supervisor then never restarts while it is high (top-level soak: c_capture_latch never hit). The LATCH_ASSERT bit is therefore never set on the chip - a design note, see the finding

AIM.16.description: Recording LATCH_ASSERT withdraws an already recorded OVP bit, treating the two latch origins as mutually exclusive in the record
AIM.16.reason: OVP captured first and latch_assert rising later in the same running episode leaves fault_reg with LATCH set and OVP cleared, although bits must only be cleared by a host read.

judgements.reason: With fault_reg holding only BIT_OVP, a new live cause makes episode_start true in the mutant. Line 166 then re-stamps fault_time, which the original holds.

decisions.reason: an episode opened by OVP alone and a UVLO record surviving a later soft start are untested; needs an OVP-only record followed by a second cause (fault_time held), and a restart after a recorded UVLO

AIM.17.description: The record is judged empty from the four lower cause bits only; a recorded OVP does not count as an open episode
AIM.17.reason: In an episode whose only recorded cause is OVP, fault_time is re-latched on every clock a cause is live, so it follows timestamp_ms or jumps to the time of a later cause instead of holding the start time.

judgements.reason: A UVLO that arrives after another cause is already recorded is dropped by the mutant, so BIT_UVLO differs.

decisions.reason: no test adds a cause after another is already recorded in the orders that matter (UVLO second, a lower-priority cause after a higher one, OVP after any cause); needs causes arriving in several orders, each checked to be added

AIM.18.description: UVLO is recorded only as the first cause of an episode; a UVLO that follows another recorded cause is treated as a consequence and dropped
AIM.18.reason: With a cause already in fault_reg and the converter still running, uvlo_state going high no longer sets fault_reg[1].

AIM.19.description: LATCH_ASSERT is recorded only once the debounced SCR readback confirms it, not when the CPLD asserts the trip
AIM.19.reason: latch_assert high while latch_state is still low (the readback lags the trip) sets no LATCH bit; if running ends before latch_state rises, fault_reg[3] is never set, while fault_time is still latched for the episode.

AIM.20.description: fault_time is cleared by a host read only when the converter is stopped; a read during S_SS or S_RUN clears fault_reg but leaves the old start time
AIM.20.reason: After a read while running with no cause live, fault_reg reads 0 but fault_time keeps the previous episode's timestamp instead of returning to 0.

AIM.21.description: The three bytes of timestamp_ms are latched into fault_time in reversed order
AIM.21.reason: fault_time at the start of any episode differs from timestamp_ms whenever the top and bottom bytes of the timestamp are not equal.

AIM.22.description: fault_time is cleared when the converter stops, instead of being held until the host reads the record
AIM.22.after: else if (episode_start)           fault_time <= timestamp_ms; / else if (!convertor_running)      fault_time <= '0;
AIM.22.reason: Once ss_active and run_active both drop after a fault, fault_time returns to 0 while fault_reg still holds the causes, so the start time is lost before the host can read it.

AIM.23.description: OVP is inferred from any disagreement between latch_state and latch_assert, not only from the latch set without the CPLD's trip
AIM.23.reason: While running, latch_assert high before the debounced latch_state reads back sets the OVP bit as well as LATCH, reporting a CPLD-originated trip as an analog overvoltage.

AIM.24.description: fault_time is re-latched every time a cause not yet in the record is captured, so it holds the time of the most recent new cause instead of the start of the episode
AIM.24.before: episode_start = convertor_running && (fault_reg == '0) / && (otp_state || uvlo_state || ovp || latch_assert / || window_trip || window_trip_SS);
AIM.24.reason: If OTP is captured while running and then a different cause such as UVLO arrives before the host reads, fault_time shows the later UVLO time instead of the OTP time. With only one cause per episode it gives the same result as the correct design.

AIM.25.description: The capture gate only scopes the start of an episode: once fault_reg holds a cause, further causes are added even after the converter has stopped
AIM.25.reason: Suppose an OTP shutdown is recorded and the converter goes to S_OFF. If UVLO then asserts during the routine power-down, or OVP or the latch asserts while stopped, the UVLO, OVP or LATCH bit is also set before the host reads, though the header says conditions arising while stopped are not captured.

AIM.26.description: Episode start leaves out the overcurrent window trips, on the assumption that an overcurrent episode only starts when latch_assert trips, so the accumulator and the episode detector disagree
AIM.26.reason: If the first cause of an episode is a window_trip in S_RUN or a window_trip_SS in S_SS, the OVERCURRENT bit is set but fault_time stays 0. Because fault_reg is then no longer empty, a later OTP, UVLO or latch cause in the same episode does not latch the start time either.

AIM.27.description: fault_time records when the converter stopped with a non-empty record (the shutdown) instead of when the first cause of the episode was captured
AIM.27.before: episode_start = convertor_running && (fault_reg == '0) / && (otp_state || uvlo_state || ovp || latch_assert / || window_trip || window_trip_SS);
AIM.27.reason: If a cause is captured in S_SS or S_RUN and the converter then stops, fault_time holds the timestamp of the first stopped clock instead of the first cause's clock; if the converter keeps running after the cause, fault_time stays 0 until it stops.

AIM.28.description: A host read stamps fault_time with the read time instead of clearing it, so an empty record reports when it was last read
AIM.28.reason: After any host read with no new episode following it, fault_time reads as the timestamp of the read instead of 0; an empty fault_reg no longer goes with a zero fault_time.

AIM.29.description: Cause bit positions laid out LSB-first (OVP in bit 0, OVERCURRENT in bit 4), with the priority order misremembered as LSB highest
AIM.29.before: localparam int BIT_OVP   = 4; / localparam int BIT_LATCH = 3; / localparam int BIT_OTP   = 2; / localparam int BIT_UVLO  = 1; / localparam int BIT_OC    = 0;
AIM.29.after: localparam int BIT_OVP   = 0; / localparam int BIT_LATCH = 1; / localparam int BIT_OTP   = 2; / localparam int BIT_UVLO  = 3; / localparam int BIT_OC    = 4;
AIM.29.reason: Any recorded OVP, LATCH_ASSERT, UVLO or overcurrent cause appears in the wrong bit of fault_reg: an overcurrent window trip during S_RUN sets bit 4, which the host reads as OVP.
AIM.29.withdrawn: another relabelling of the cause bit map; the adjacent swaps AIM.36, AIM.38, AIM.47 and AIM.49 already move every cause, and any test that checks each cause on its own bit kills them all

AIM.30.description: fault_reg is cleared when the converter stops, like the supervisor's window state, instead of being held until the host reads it
AIM.30.after: else if(!convertor_running) begin / fault_reg <= '0; / end / else begin
AIM.30.reason: After a fault shuts the converter down (S_RUN or S_SS to stopped), fault_reg reads back as 0 one clock later, so the cause of the shutdown is lost while fault_time still holds the episode start.

AIM.31.description: While running, any live cause overwrites the record with a snapshot of the currently live causes instead of OR-accumulating into it
AIM.31.before: if(otp_state)                       fault_reg[BIT_OTP]   <= 1'b1; / if(uvlo_state)                      fault_reg[BIT_UVLO]  <= 1'b1; / if(window_trip || window_trip_SS)   fault_reg [BIT_OC]   <= 1'b1; / if(ovp)                             fault_reg[BIT_OVP]   <= 1'b1; / if(latch_assert)                    fault_reg[BIT_LATCH] <= 1'b1;
AIM.31.after: if(otp_state || uvlo_state || ovp || latch_assert || window_trip || window_trip_SS) begin / fault_reg <= {ovp, latch_assert, otp_state, uvlo_state, (window_trip || window_trip_SS)}; / end
AIM.31.reason: If one cause (say OTP) is captured and goes away, and a different cause (say UVLO) is then live while still in S_SS/S_RUN, fault_reg loses the OTP bit and reports only UVLO.

AIM.32.description: The accumulator's capture gate is S_RUN only, while episode_start still uses convertor_running (S_SS or S_RUN), so the two blocks no longer agree during soft start
AIM.32.reason: A cause that is live during soft start (for example window_trip_SS or OTP while ss_active) is not recorded in fault_reg. Because fault_reg stays empty, episode_start fires on every clock, so fault_time keeps following timestamp_ms while fault_reg reads 0.

AIM.33.description: OVERCURRENT is recorded only when the window trip has already led to a CPLD latch trip, as if an overcurrent only counts once strikes reach the trip
AIM.33.reason: A window_trip or window_trip_SS that does not (yet) assert latch_assert, i.e. one strike below the limit, leaves bit 0 of fault_reg clear. The original records it on the first window trip.

judgements.reason: A latch_assert during ss_active only sets BIT_LATCH in the original but not in the mutant.

decisions.reason: need latch_assert high while the converter runs, which never happens on the chip: strike_counter raises latch_assert on hiccup entry, after S_RUN has been left, and the supervisor then never restarts while it is high (top-level soak: c_capture_latch never hit). The LATCH_ASSERT bit is therefore never set on the chip - a design note, see the finding

AIM.34.description: LATCH_ASSERT is recorded only in S_RUN, on the assumption that the CPLD trips the latch only from run-time strikes, so a latch trip during soft start is forgotten
AIM.34.reason: If latch_assert rises while ss_active is high (an overcurrent in soft start), bit 3 of fault_reg is not set. The original records it whenever the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN.

AIM.35.description: A soft-start overcurrent window trip is filed under the LATCH_ASSERT (OCP/SCP) bit instead of the OVERCURRENT bit
AIM.35.before: if(window_trip || window_trip_SS)   fault_reg [BIT_OC]   <= 1'b1; / if(ovp)                             fault_reg[BIT_OVP]   <= 1'b1; / if(latch_assert)                    fault_reg[BIT_LATCH] <= 1'b1;
AIM.35.after: if(window_trip)                     fault_reg [BIT_OC]   <= 1'b1; / if(ovp)                             fault_reg[BIT_OVP]   <= 1'b1; / if(latch_assert || window_trip_SS)  fault_reg[BIT_LATCH] <= 1'b1;
AIM.35.reason: When window_trip_SS asserts during soft start with latch_assert low, fault_reg reads 01000 instead of 00001.

AIM.36.description: The OTP and UVLO cause bits are laid out in swapped positions, with the priority order between them misremembered
AIM.36.before: localparam int BIT_OTP   = 2; / localparam int BIT_UVLO  = 1;
AIM.36.after: localparam int BIT_OTP   = 1; / localparam int BIT_UVLO  = 2;
AIM.36.reason: An over-temperature while running sets fault_reg bit 1 instead of bit 2, and an undervoltage sets bit 2 instead of bit 1, so the host reads 00010 for OTP and 00100 for UVLO.

judgements.reason: An inferred ovp during ss_active only sets BIT_OVP in the original but not in the mutant.

decisions.reason: no cause is raised during soft start: OTP, UVLO and OVP captured in S_SS, the episode stamp from S_SS and a second cause in S_SS are untested; needs causes in S_SS with fault_reg and fault_time checked

AIM.37.description: OVP is recorded only in S_RUN, on the assumption that overvoltage can only occur once the output is regulated, so an OVP overshoot during soft start is not recorded
AIM.37.reason: An analog OVP trip (latch_state high, latch_assert low) during S_SS leaves fault_reg[4] clear. episode_start still fires on ovp, so fault_time is latched while fault_reg reads empty.

AIM.38.description: The OVP and LATCH_ASSERT cause bits are laid out in swapped positions, with the CPLD's measured trip misremembered as outranking the inferred OVP
AIM.38.before: localparam int BIT_OVP   = 4; / localparam int BIT_LATCH = 3;
AIM.38.after: localparam int BIT_OVP   = 3; / localparam int BIT_LATCH = 4;
AIM.38.reason: An analog OVP trip while running sets fault_reg bit 3 (10000 expected, 01000 read), and a latch_assert captured while running sets bit 4, so the host reads the wrong cause.

AIM.39.description: OVP is inferred with the two latch signals confused: CPLD trip asserted while the SCR readback is still clear, instead of readback set without a CPLD trip
AIM.39.reason: An analog OVP trip while running (latch_state high, latch_assert low) no longer sets fault_reg[4] or opens an episode. A CPLD trip seen while running before the debounced readback follows is wrongly recorded as OVP.

judgements.reason: With the converter stopped and latch_assert=1, the mutant captures latch_assert and any other live causes into fault_reg. The original records nothing.

decisions.reason: nothing is raised while the converter is stopped: the header says a fault asserting while stopped is not captured and the record holds until read, but no test raises latch_state, latch_assert or OTP (or lets OTP clear) with the converter stopped and checks fault_reg and fault_time stay as they were

AIM.40.description: The capture gate is held open while the CPLD's latch trip is asserted, so the trip that stops the converter is sure to be seen. Because latch_assert is held until reset, the gate never closes after a latch trip.
AIM.40.reason: latch_assert stays high until rst_n after a strike-out trip, while the supervisor sits in S_OFF. If the host reads fault_reg in that state, the original stays empty, but the mutant sets LATCH_ASSERT again on the next clock. Any OTP or UVLO that arrives later, such as a power-down UVLO, is also recorded.

AIM.41.description: A host read clears fault_time only when no cause is live. The episode is treated as still open while any cause persists, so its start time survives the read even though fault_reg is cleared.
AIM.41.after: else if (fault_reg_read_done && !(otp_state || uvlo_state || ovp || latch_assert / || window_trip || window_trip_SS)) fault_time <= '0;
AIM.41.reason: After a latch trip, latch_assert stays high with the converter stopped. A host read then empties fault_reg, and in the original fault_time goes to 0. In the mutant fault_time keeps the old episode start time next to an empty fault_reg, and no new episode can re-stamp it while the converter is stopped.

AIM.42.description: The LATCH_ASSERT bit is set whenever the protection latch reads back set, so an analog OVP trip is recorded as both OVP and LATCH_ASSERT (OCP/SCP)
AIM.42.reason: Suppose an analog OVP trips the shared latch during S_SS or S_RUN while latch_assert stays low. fault_reg should read 10000 but reads 11000, which reports an overcurrent trip that never happened.

AIM.43.description: OVP is inferred as a latch trip with no recorded overcurrent, as if every CPLD trip is shown by a recorded window trip, instead of a latch trip without the CPLD's latch_assert
AIM.43.reason: Suppose a host read clears the OVERCURRENT bit and the strikes then reach a CPLD latch trip while the converter is running. The OVP bit is set wrongly. In the other direction, an analog OVP trip in an episode that has already recorded a window trip leaves the OVP bit clear.

AIM.44.description: fault_time is re-latched whenever a live cause outranks every cause already recorded, so it gives the time of the highest-priority cause instead of the start of the episode
AIM.44.before: episode_start = convertor_running && (fault_reg == '0) / && (otp_state || uvlo_state || ovp || latch_assert / || window_trip || window_trip_SS);
AIM.44.after: episode_start = convertor_running / && ({ovp, latch_assert, otp_state, uvlo_state, / (window_trip || window_trip_SS)} > fault_reg);
AIM.44.reason: Suppose a window trip opens an episode in S_RUN and an OTP or a latch trip follows it while the converter is still running. fault_time moves to the time of the later cause, where it should keep the time the episode began.

AIM.45.description: fault_reg is cleared all through soft start, as if each restart began a new record, as well as on a host read
AIM.45.reason: After a hiccup or other restart, the causes recorded in the previous episode are wiped as soon as the converter enters S_SS, before the host has read them. Causes that occur during soft start (OTP, UVLO, a window_trip_SS) also never appear in fault_reg until S_RUN.

judgements.reason: While running, if otp_state=1 and uvlo_state=1, the mutant does not set BIT_OTP.

decisions.reason: no test raises two causes on the same clock: each cause is recorded alone, so a cause masked by another live cause goes unseen; needs simultaneous pairs of causes with every bit checked

AIM.46.description: OTP is recorded only when UVLO is not live, as if a brown-out made the OTP reading unreliable and UVLO took precedence
AIM.46.reason: If OTP and UVLO are both asserted while the converter is running, and OTP clears before UVLO, fault_reg shows only the UVLO bit and the OTP cause is lost.

AIM.48.reason: On the clock after fault_reg_read_done, fault_reg is already zero but fault_time still holds the previous episode's start time. It clears only one clock later, so for that one clock the outputs give an empty record with a non-zero time.

AIM.49.description: The LATCH_ASSERT and OTP cause bits are laid out in swapped positions, so OTP is ranked above the CPLD's latch trip
AIM.49.before: localparam int BIT_LATCH = 3; / localparam int BIT_OTP   = 2;
AIM.49.after: localparam int BIT_LATCH = 2; / localparam int BIT_OTP   = 3;
AIM.49.reason: An OTP while running sets fault_reg bit 3 instead of bit 2, and a CPLD latch trip sets bit 2 instead of bit 3, so the host decodes each of these causes as the other.

AIM.50.description: The capture gate closes as soon as the protection latch reads back set, treating a set latch as a converter that has already stopped
AIM.50.reason: An analog OVP trip while running (latch_state high, latch_assert low) is never recorded in fault_reg bit 4. episode_start still fires, so fault_time keeps being re-latched while the record stays empty. Causes that arrive after a CPLD trip's readback follows are also dropped.

AIM.51.description: The OVP bit is recorded from the raw latch readback instead of the inferred ovp, so every CPLD-originated latch trip is also recorded as OVP
AIM.51.reason: After an overcurrent CPLD trip while running, once the SCR readback follows latch_assert, fault_reg shows OVP (bit 4) as well as LATCH_ASSERT (bit 3), even though no analog overvoltage happened.

decisions.reason: nothing is raised while the converter is stopped: the header says a fault asserting while stopped is not captured and the record holds until read, but no test raises latch_state, latch_assert or OTP (or lets OTP clear) with the converter stopped and checks fault_reg and fault_time stay as they were

AIM.52.description: OVP is recorded even while the converter is stopped, on the assumption that the analog comparator can trip the latch at any time and should always be logged
AIM.52.after: end /  / else if(ovp) begin /  / fault_reg[BIT_OVP] <= 1'b1; /  / end
AIM.52.reason: If the latch is set by an analog trip and the converter is stopped, a host read does not leave the record empty: bit 4 is set again on the next clock. episode_start does not fire, so fault_time stays 0 next to a non-empty record.

AIM.53.reason: When window trips run up strikes until the CPLD asserts latch_assert while running, fault_reg ends up with only bit 3 set. The OVERCURRENT bit 0, recorded earlier, is lost, although bits are meant never to be cleared individually.

AIM.54.description: The capture gate is closed whenever UVLO is live, so every UVLO is treated as a routine power-down rather than only the ones that come after the converter has stopped
AIM.54.reason: If UVLO asserts while the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN, the UVLO bit is never set. AIM.55.reason: A UVLO that interrupts S_RUN leaves the UVLO bit clear in fault_reg. If UVLO is the only cause, the record stays empty, but fault_time is still latched because episode_start still counts uvlo_state. A UVLO during S_SS is recorded as before.

AIM.56.reason: If otp_state asserts while ss_active is high and run_active is low, the OTP bit is not set. episode_start still fires on otp_state, so fault_time is stamped while fault_reg stays empty, or holds only the other causes.

AIM.59.reason: Suppose a record from an earlier episode has not been read when the converter restarts: its fault_time drops to 0 during S_SS. A first cause captured during soft start is also left with fault_time 0, because the stamp is cleared and no new episode starts afterwards.

AIM.60.reason: Example: an OTP or soft-start overcurrent is recorded and not yet read, the converter restarts, and then the analog OVP trips the latch while it is running. fault_reg[OVP] never sets, so the shutdown cause is missing from the record.

AIM.61.reason: After the converter has stopped, firmware's normal read returns the record, but fault_reg keeps its bits instead of clearing. fault_time is cleared by the same read, so a non-empty record is left with fault_time 0.

AIM.63.reason: Suppose uvlo_state asserts while the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN and the debounced latch readback is set, from either an OVP or a CPLD trip. The UVLO bit is then never set in fault_reg, though the other cause bits are still recorded.

AIM.64.reason: When window_trip_SS asserts with ss_active high, the OVERCURRENT bit is not set and fault_time is not latched (episode_start is also gated), so fault_reg and fault_time stay empty where the original records bit 0 and the timestamp; any other cause live on that clock is lost too.

AIM.67.reason: If latch_assert asserts while ss_active and run_active are both low (e.g. on a hiccup entry), fault_reg bit 3 becomes set where the original leaves fault_reg empty. A host read then cannot clear it while latch_assert is held, because it is set again on the next clock.

AIM.71.reason: After reset or after a host read with no cause live, fault_time reports the running ms count instead of 0. An empty record then shows a non-zero, changing start time.

AIM.75.reason: If OTP is recorded, the converter stops, the board cools and the supervisor restarts into S_SS before any host read, the OTP bit in fault_reg is cleared, although the header says bits are never cleared one at a time.

judgements.reason: While running, if uvlo_state is high together with window_trip or window_trip_SS, the mutant does not set BIT_UVLO.

AIM.76.description: UVLO is not recorded while an overcurrent window trip is live, on the belief that an input droop under overcurrent is caused by the load current
AIM.76.reason: With the converter in S_SS or S_RUN, a UVLO that is asserted only while window_trip or window_trip_SS is high leaves fault_reg[1] clear, but OVERCURRENT is still recorded.

AIM.77.reason: When a window trip records OVERCURRENT and latch_assert rises on a later clock while the converter still runs, fault_reg[3] stays clear, so the OCP/SCP trip is missing from the record.

AIM.78.description: fault_time stamps the converter's soft start, read as the start of an operating episode, instead of the capture of the first fault cause
AIM.78.before: episode_start = convertor_running && (fault_reg == '0) / && (otp_state || uvlo_state || ovp || latch_assert / || window_trip || window_trip_SS);

With this fault, fault_reg[BIT_UVLO] is set while fault_time stays 0, because episode_start is still gated. A later real fault during run then finds the record non-empty and is never time-stamped.

AIM.89.description: When deciding whether the record is empty, the episode detector ignores the UVLO bit, as if a recorded UVLO were the routine power-down the capture gate is there to ignore and did not open an episode
AIM.89.reason: If a UVLO is recorded while the converter is running, and later (with no host read in between) another cause is captured during S_SS or S_RUN, fault_time is re-latched to the later time. The header says fault_time should keep the time the UVLO episode began.

judgements.reason: While running, if otp_state=1 together with latch_state=1 and latch_assert=0, the mutant does not infer ovp. BIT_OVP is not recorded at line 208.

decisions.reason: no test raises two causes on the same clock: each cause is recorded alone, so a cause masked by another live cause goes unseen; needs simultaneous pairs of causes with every bit checked

AIM.90.description: OVP inference is suppressed while OTP is live, as if the over-temperature comparator were a third trip source of the shared protection latch
AIM.90.reason: If the latch reads back set without latch_assert during S_SS or S_RUN while otp_state is high, the OVP bit (bit 4) of fault_reg is not set. If the record was empty and OTP was the only other live cause, fault_time is still latched, but bit 4 is missing.

AIM.91.description: OTP is not recorded once OVERCURRENT is in the record, on the belief that an over-temperature after an overcurrent is only the heating the overcurrent caused
AIM.91.reason: Sequence: a window trip records OVERCURRENT, the hiccup retry restarts the converter, and then otp_state rises during S_SS or S_RUN, all with no host read in between. The OTP bit (bit 2) of fault_reg stays clear, when the header requires every cause seen while running to be accumulated.

AIM.92.description: When deciding whether the record is empty, the episode detector ignores the OTP bit, as if a self-clearing over-temperature that has cooled off did not hold an episode open
AIM.92.reason: After an OTP is recorded at T1 and the board cools, the converter restarts; a later cause (e.g. UVLO or a window trip) captured before any host read re-stamps fault_time with its own time instead of keeping T1.

judgements.reason: While running, if uvlo_state and otp_state are both high, the mutant does not set BIT_UVLO.

decisions.reason: no test raises two causes on the same clock: each cause is recorded alone, so a cause masked by another live cause goes unseen; needs simultaneous pairs of causes with every bit checked

AIM.93.description: UVLO is not recorded while OTP is live, as if over-temperature outranked and explained a simultaneous input brown-out
AIM.93.reason: If OTP and UVLO both assert on the same clock while the converter is running (it stops on the next clock), fault_reg reports only OTP instead of OTP and UVLO.

judgements.reason: While running, if a window trip happens together with uvlo_state=1, the mutant does not set BIT_OC.

decisions.reason: no test raises two causes on the same clock: each cause is recorded alone, so a cause masked by another live cause goes unseen; needs simultaneous pairs of causes with every bit checked

AIM.94.description: The OVERCURRENT bit is not recorded while UVLO is live, on the belief that a window trip during a brown-out is only the input-current surge the droop causes
AIM.94.reason: A window trip (S_RUN) or soft-start window trip that coincides with UVLO while the converter is running sets only the UVLO bit; the OVERCURRENT bit stays clear in the read-back.

judgements.reason: Once BIT_UVLO is recorded, a later clock with ss_active=1 and uvlo_state=0 clears it in the mutant. The original never clears individual bits.

decisions.reason: an episode opened by OVP alone and a UVLO record surviving a later soft start are untested; needs an OVP-only record followed by a second cause (fault_time held), and a restart after a recorded UVLO

AIM.95.description: The UVLO bit is withdrawn during soft start once Vin is back. A restart after a recovered brown-out is taken to mean the UVLO was a routine power cycle and not a fault.
AIM.95.reason: Suppose UVLO is recorded while running, the converter stops, and it later re-enters S_SS with uvlo_state low. fault_reg[1] is then cleared before the host reads it, so the brown-out that interrupted operation is missing from the record. The same happens to a UVLO that interrupts soft start once it clears.

judgements.reason: A read while the converter is stopped and fault_time is non-zero clears fault_time in the original. The mutant leaves it unchanged.

decisions.reason: host reads are only tested while running with causes gone: a read on the clock the first cause is captured, a read while stopped, and a read of an empty record with a cause live are untested

AIM.96.description: A host read clears fault_time only while the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN. A read after a shutdown clears fault_reg but leaves the old episode start time.
AIM.96.reason: After a fault stops the converter, the host reads the record. fault_reg reads back as zero, but fault_time keeps the previous episode's timestamp instead of 0. It stays wrong until a new episode overwrites it.

AIM.97.description: Over-temperature (OT) and over-current (OC) are confused in the bit map: OTP is placed in bit 0 and OVERCURRENT in bit 2
AIM.97.before: localparam int BIT_OTP   = 2; / localparam int BIT_UVLO  = 1; / localparam int BIT_OC    = 0;
AIM.97.after: localparam int BIT_OTP   = 0; / localparam int BIT_UVLO  = 1; / localparam int BIT_OC    = 2;
AIM.97.reason: An OTP during S_SS or S_RUN sets fault_reg bit 0 instead of bit 2, and an overcurrent window trip sets bit 2 instead of bit 0. Firmware then decodes an overheated board as an overcurrent, and the reverse.
AIM.97.withdrawn: another relabelling of the cause bit map; the adjacent swaps AIM.36, AIM.38, AIM.47 and AIM.49 already move every cause, and any test that checks each cause on its own bit kills them all

AIM.98.description: The two lock-type causes are confused in the bit map: the CPLD latch trip (LATCH_ASSERT) is placed in bit 1 and under-voltage lockout (UVLO) in bit 3
AIM.98.before: localparam int BIT_LATCH = 3; / localparam int BIT_OTP   = 2; / localparam int BIT_UVLO  = 1;
AIM.98.after: localparam int BIT_LATCH = 1; / localparam int BIT_OTP   = 2; / localparam int BIT_UVLO  = 3;
AIM.98.reason: A latch_assert trip while the converter runs sets fault_reg bit 1 instead of bit 3, and a UVLO sets bit 3 instead of bit 1. Firmware reports an OCP/SCP latch trip as a brown-out, and the reverse.
AIM.98.withdrawn: another relabelling of the cause bit map; the adjacent swaps AIM.36, AIM.38, AIM.47 and AIM.49 already move every cause, and any test that checks each cause on its own bit kills them all

AIM.99.description: A host read acknowledges only the highest-priority recorded cause and leaves the lower-priority causes in the record, instead of clearing the whole record
AIM.99.after: if(fault_reg[BIT_OVP])             fault_reg[BIT_OVP]   <= 1'b0; / else if(fault_reg[BIT_LATCH])      fault_reg[BIT_LATCH] <= 1'b0; / else if(fault_reg[BIT_OTP])        fault_reg[BIT_OTP]   <= 1'b0; / else if(fault_reg[BIT_UVLO])       fault_reg[BIT_UVLO]  <= 1'b0; / else                               fault_reg[BIT_OC]    <= 1'b0;
AIM.99.reason: Suppose a record holds two causes, for example OTP and OVERCURRENT, and the host reads it after the converter has stopped. fault_reg still shows OVERCURRENT after the read, although it should be empty. fault_time is cleared, so the remaining record has no start time.

judgements.reason: With fault_reg empty, if UVLO is the only cause during ss_active, the mutant does not assert episode_start. fault_time stays 0 while fault_reg[BIT_UVLO] is set.

decisions.reason: no cause is raised during soft start: OTP, UVLO and OVP captured in S_SS, the episode stamp from S_SS and a second cause in S_SS are untested; needs causes in S_SS with fault_reg and fault_time checked

AIM.100.description: UVLO opens an episode only in S_RUN: a Vin dip during soft start is treated as inrush sag and does not stamp fault_time, although the accumulator still records it
AIM.100.reason: Suppose UVLO is the first cause, and it asserts during S_SS. fault_reg gets the UVLO bit, but fault_time stays zero instead of taking timestamp_ms. Later causes do not stamp it either, because the record is no longer empty.

AIM.101.description: The capture gate is held open while the over-temperature comparator is asserted, so that an OTP the supervisor stops on is sure to be recorded. The gate then stays open after the stop for as long as the board stays hot.
AIM.101.reason: Suppose the converter has stopped while otp_state is still high. A routine power-down UVLO in that time is recorded, which it should not be. A host read clears the record, but OTP then sets its own bit again and episode_start stamps a new fault_time. In the original, both stay empty.

AIM.102.description: A host read leaves the UVLO bit in place, as if it were a sticky brown-out status flag that only rst_n clears, while every other cause bit is cleared.
AIM.102.reason: If a host reads a record that holds UVLO, fault_reg still reads back with bit 1 set after the read. Because the record never looks empty again, a later fault never fires episode_start, and fault_time stays at the 0 the read wrote.

AIM.103.description: The OVERCURRENT bit is cleared whenever the converter is stopped, copying the fault_arbiter window's reset on leaving S_RUN/S_SS into the record, so an overcurrent that stopped the converter is gone from the record
AIM.103.reason: After a window_trip or window_trip_SS stops the converter (hiccup or fault state), fault_reg[0] drops to 0 on the next clock. A host read after the shutdown then shows no OVERCURRENT, while fault_time still holds the start of the episode.

judgements.reason: With the converter stopped, no read pending and otp_state=0, the new else branch clears a recorded BIT_OTP. The original holds it.

decisions.reason: nothing is raised while the converter is stopped: the header says a fault asserting while stopped is not captured and the record holds until read, but no test raises latch_state, latch_assert or OTP (or lets OTP clear) with the converter stopped and checks fault_reg and fault_time stay as they were

AIM.104.description: Once the converter has stopped, the OTP bit is withdrawn as soon as the board cools, as if a self-clearing over-temperature should clear its own record before the next start
AIM.104.after: end /  / else begin / if(!otp_state)                      fault_reg[BIT_OTP]   <= 1'b0; / end
AIM.104.reason: An OTP captured while running stops the converter. When otp_state later deasserts with the converter still stopped, fault_reg[2] falls to 0, so a host read after the board has cooled does not show the cause that stopped the converter.

AIM.105.description: A host read leaves the OTP bit in place, treating it as a latched thermal-shutdown flag that only rst_n clears, while every other cause bit is cleared
AIM.105.reason: After an OTP has been recorded and the board has cooled, a host read clears fault_time and the other bits but fault_reg[2] stays at 1. Every later read still reports over-temperature until reset.

AIM.106.description: The capture gate closes as soon as the CPLD asserts latch_assert, treating the CPLD's own trip into the latch as a converter that has already stopped
AIM.106.reason: When latch_assert rises while the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN, fault_reg[BIT_LATCH] is never set. If no other cause is live, fault_time is not stamped. latch_assert is held until reset, so every later cause is also dropped from fault_reg.

AIM.107.description: A host read leaves the OVERCURRENT bit in place, treating the window-trip record like the strike history that only a long clean run or rst_n clears, while every other cause bit is cleared
AIM.107.reason: After an overcurrent window trip has been recorded, a host read should return fault_reg to zero. With this fault it stays at 5'b00001, so the next read still reports OVERCURRENT, and a later cause no longer counts as the start of an episode, so fault_time stays zero.

judgements.reason: With ss_active=run_active=0 and latch_state=1, the mutant opens the gate at line 104. Causes are then captured at lines 205-209 and fault_time is stamped at line 166, but the original records nothing while stopped.

decisions.reason: nothing is raised while the converter is stopped: the header says a fault asserting while stopped is not captured and the record holds until read, but no test raises latch_state, latch_assert or OTP (or lets OTP clear) with the converter stopped and checks fault_reg and fault_time stay as they were

AIM.108.description: The capture gate is held open while the protection latch reads back set, so that the analog OVP trip that stops the converter is sure to be recorded
AIM.108.reason: latch_state stays high until reset, so after an analog OVP trip the gate never closes. A UVLO or OTP that asserts after the converter has stopped is then recorded, and after a host read the still-live ovp sets the OVP bit again and stamps a new fault_time, so the record never stays clear.

AIM.109.description: fault_reg is cleared when it sees fault_time already cleared and the record non-empty, so its clear follows the read pulse through fault_time instead of using the pulse itself
AIM.109.reason: The record is cleared one clock after the read. A cause that asserts on the clock after the read is lost, because the late clear outranks capture on that clock. A record whose episode began while timestamp_ms was still 0 is also wiped on the next clock without any host read.

AIM.110.description: Causes are recorded only on the clock the episode opens. A cause that appears later in the same episode is never added to fault_reg.
AIM.110.reason: While the converter is running with OTP already recorded, a later latch_assert or window trip does not set its bit. fault_reg reads only the first cause instead of all the causes OR-accumulated over the episode.

AIM.111.description: While the converter runs, the UVLO bit follows the live debounced UVLO instead of being set and held
AIM.111.reason: Suppose uvlo_state pulses high and then drops while ss_active or run_active stays high (a Vin dip that recovers). The UVLO bit in fault_reg clears again, but fault_time still holds the start time the dip stamped.

AIM.112.description: The over-temperature and over-voltage trips are confused: an inferred analog OVP trip is also recorded as OTP
AIM.112.reason: While running, if latch_state goes high with latch_assert low, fault_reg reads OVP|OTP (10100) instead of OVP alone (10000), even though otp_state never asserted.

AIM.113.description: Every S_RUN window trip is also recorded as LATCH_ASSERT (OCP/SCP), as if each window trip were an OCP trip into the latch
AIM.113.reason: In S_RUN, a window_trip that never builds up enough strikes to raise latch_assert sets fault_reg to 01001 instead of 00001, so it reports a CPLD latch trip that did not happen.

AIM.114.description: Each overcurrent window trip is qualified with the other trip's supervisor state: the S_RUN window_trip is accepted only during soft start and window_trip_SS only in S_RUN
AIM.114.reason: An overcurrent window trip in S_RUN, or a soft-start window trip in S_SS, no longer sets the OVERCURRENT bit. Episode start still sees it, so fault_time is stamped while fault_reg stays empty or lacks bit 0.

judgements.reason: While running, if otp_state=1 and latch_state=1, the mutant does not set BIT_OTP.

decisions.reason: no test raises two causes on the same clock: each cause is recorded alone, so a cause masked by another live cause goes unseen; needs simultaneous pairs of causes with every bit checked

AIM.115.description: OTP is not recorded while the protection latch reads back set, on the belief that a latched converter is no longer heating the board, so any over-temperature then is not part of the fault
AIM.115.reason: If an over-temperature is asserted while the converter is still running and the SCR readback is set (an analog OVP or CPLD trip not yet acted on by the supervisor), the OTP bit stays clear in fault_reg. The original records it.

AIM.116.description: OVP is recorded only during soft start, on the belief that an analog overvoltage can only be the overshoot at the end of the soft-start ramp, so an OVP trip in S_RUN (a load dump, say) is not recorded
AIM.116.reason: If the analog comparator trips the latch while run_active is high and latch_assert is low, bit 4 of fault_reg stays clear. fault_time is still stamped because episode_start fires, so the host reads a timestamp with no cause bit set. An OVP during S_SS is still recorded.

AIM.117.description: A host read clears only the top byte of fault_time (FTIME_2, the byte whose read raises the pulse), so the two low bytes keep the old episode start time
AIM.117.reason: After the host reads a record whose start time had non-zero low bytes, fault_time reads back non-zero (the old low 16 bits) while fault_reg is empty. This lasts until the next episode re-stamps it, but the header says fault_time is cleared with the bits.

AIM.118.description: Episode start is detected only during soft start, as if every fault episode began with a failed start-up, so a first cause captured in S_RUN does not stamp fault_time
AIM.118.reason: A first fault that appears while the converter is in S_RUN (OTP, UVLO, a window trip or a latch trip) is still recorded in fault_reg, but fault_time stays at zero instead of latching timestamp_ms.
